questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I thought the city was a nice combination of a different culture but not too different so that there would be many culture shocks for me. It was also student friendly meaning not too expensive to live in as a student.
The city was placed in the centrum of Europe which gave a lot of opportunities to travel to other destinations.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough to find information but not all information was correct. For example was it stated that the semester would last until mid february however in reality it was possible to be done with the semester at before christmas.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved mostly emails with information. There was also one short information meeting before the semester started.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a personal contact.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most erasmus students live of campus. The dormitories at campus should not have the best quality.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You signed up through the universty web site after a week where you could attend all the available classes. It was a first come first served basis but it was possible to sign up for classes even if it had been filled up on the website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could attend all the available classes before signing up. There were video guides explaining the process of signing up too.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the introductions. Be ready when the registration on the website starts. Ask the professor if you can attend the class even if it is already filled up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The english level for most of the professors was not very high. This made them hard to understand. Most classes were only Erasmus students which seemed to influence how much effort was made into teaching the class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were only lecture classes no seminar classes. Almost no reading before classes. Most exams were multiple choice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Czech Constitutional Law, Private Law, Introduction to Public International Law in the Czech Legal Context, Natural Resources Law, Introduction into Central European Legal Culture, Legal Reasoning: First Amendment Case Law og Intellectual Property Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Legal Reasoning: First Amendment Case Law
Private Law
Introduction into Central European Legal Culture

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We got an e-mail about the opportunities both when we were 2 months into the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did the intensive czech course before which were a good opportunity to meet people from other faculties too.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on trips in Czech Republic the bus tickets are were cheap. Go travel to the cities close to Prague.
Visit the national teater students get a discount.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The english level was not very high especially going grocery shopping was difficult. But Prague is a very well-functioning city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some classes were local students attend. Get a "buddy" that the university offers.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Czech people are not very outgoing when it comes to international people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Much consideration was given to students, especially when it comes to prices.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The city is very easy to live in, the public transportation is great.
if you want to travel in your semester the location is great.
Do not expect the locals to understand english.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not worry about information it will usually come last minut no matter what you do.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting students from other countries. Trying to live in a new city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not always feeling welcome in Prague

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you consider going on an exhange do it, it is a great experience and opportunity.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
